QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_26

question.text: Ms. Anita Kapoor, LP in 'Mumbai Category II AIF', has a side-letter with a 'Most Favoured Nation' (MFN) provision. This entitles her to:

answer.text: Elect the benefit of rights contained in other investors' side-letters (and potentially also the right to view those side-letters)
First access to any new scheme launched by the Sponsor

explanation.text: The Logic: An MFN provision entitles the investor to ELECT the benefit of rights granted to other investors in THEIR side-letters, and potentially the right to view those side-letters. It's an equal-treatment mechanism that prevents arbitrary privileges. The PDF stresses that MFN usage should be 'regularised'. The Trap: First access is a capacity right, not MFN. Guaranteed return is prohibited in AIF structure. Veto on investment is an IC member right. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests MFN. XIX-A Distributor may mention MFN conceptually. Manager's Pro-Tip: MFN is double-edged — giving one LP an unusual term means the MFN-LPs can all claim it. In practice, segment MFN into 'benefits with thresholds' (e.g., only LPs above INR 25 crore can elect rights given to LPs above INR 50 crore).
